open_theses.question: Will NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra rack-scale platform — the Kyber NVL144 architecture that houses 144 Rubin Ultra GPUs — reach first shipments in 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
open_theses.outcome: Whether NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra rack platform reaches first shipments (the step that brings revenue) in 2027 or is delayed to 2028.

open_theses.question: What will the outstanding amount of NVIDIA's supply (purchase) commitments to suppliers be at its next annual report — the obligations that lock it into buying capacity and services for its AI systems?
open_theses.outcome: The outstanding supply/purchase commitments disclosed in NVIDIA's next annual report, compared with the $119 billion cited in this item.

open_theses.question: How much revenue will the big four hyperscalers' in-house AI accelerators (Amazon Trainium, Google TPU, Microsoft Maia, Meta MTIA) generate in calendar 2026 — the combined custom-silicon quantity competing with NVIDIA GPUs, whose customers also fund NVIDIA's data center segment?
open_theses.outcome: The combined calendar-2026 revenue (or disclosed shipment volume) of the four hyperscalers' in-house AI accelerator programmes, as disclosed in their full-year 2026 results and earnings calls.

open_theses.question: What share of Chinese enterprises' AI accelerator budget will be allocated to domestic (Chinese-made) products versus Nvidia over the 12 months following the July 2026 survey, and will it rise toward the 46% executives indicated from 30% today?
open_theses.outcome: The share of surveyed Chinese enterprise AI accelerator budget going to domestic products — and by implication Nvidia's remaining share — over the 12 months after the July 2026 survey.
